newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan wants to send Lien to APEC summit - report.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan wants to send Lien to APEC summit - report.

text.p: Taiwan is hoping to send vice-president Lien Chan to represent President Lee Teng-hui at next month's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum meeting in the Philippines, the Liberty Times reported on Sunday.
An envoy of Philippine President Fidel Ramos has told Taiwan Manila would not invite Lee to attend the meeting of APEC leaders on November 25, the independent newspaper said.

However, the paper quoted unindentified government sources as saying Manila has promised to upgrade Taiwan's representation in the key forum to allow either Lien, who doubles as premier, or his deputy, vice-premier Hsu Li-teh, to attend.
Lien was elected vice-president in March as running mate of President Lee in a historic election that gave both their first popular mandate.

If Lien or Hsu attended, they would be the most senior Taiwan officials to take part in an annual APEC leaders' summit. Their presence at the meeting would likely provoke China, which has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a civil war separated them in 1949.
Taiwan government officials were not available for comment on Sunday.
Beijing insists Taipei is not entitled to any international recognition and demands Lee not be accorded the status of a national leader at any international or bilateral meetings.
Taiwan officials, however, have repeatedly said the APEC summit would be an ideal place for an historic meeting between Lee and China's President Jiang Zemin.

Lee made a private, but high-profile, visit to the United States in June 1995. A furious Beijing had said the visit showed that Lee wanted Taiwan's independence and not reunification with the mainland.
Foreign ministry spokesman Peter Cheng said last week that the government would continue to fight for President Lee's presence at the summit.
China, Taiwan and Hong Kong joined APEC in 1991 but Taipei and Hong Kong agreed to send only economic ministers to the forum, which groups 18 Pacific Rim countries.

Taiwan sent its top China negotiator, Koo Chen-fu, to attend the APEC summit in Japan in 1995 and Vincent Siew, who was then chairman of the island's top economic planning agency, to take part in the 1994 APEC summit meeting in Indonesia.

APEC members are Australia, the United States, Canada, Chile Mexico, Japan, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea, Indonesia, Brunei, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Papua New Guinea and New Zealand.
